newsitem.title: INDIA: Political worries drag India rupee down vs fwd dlr.
newsitem.headline: Political worries drag India rupee down vs fwd dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened on Thursday against the forward dollar on political uncertainties arising from the Congress Party's withdrawal of support to the ruling United Front governemnt, dealers said.
United Front leader Laloo Yadav told reporters he expected fresh elections to Parliament soon as talks with the Congress Party had failed.
"This led to paying pressure (paying premiums to buy forward dollars), pushing up premiums," said a bank dealer.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed Thursday at 6.36 percent, up from the previous close of 5.92 percent.
Some dealers described the rise in premium as a welcome correction, saying it had touched unrealistically low levels.
The spot rupee which had threatened to harden to 35.82 level was kept under leash by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases at 35.83 on Thursday, dealers said.
The RBI intervention scotched speculation in some quarters that excess liquidity in the money market had become a larger issue for the central bank than the exchange rate.
RBI had not intervened in the market on Wednesday.
The spot rupee saw a high of 35.830 and a low of 35.852 against the dollar on Thursday, dealers said.
